developments.title: Leonie announces release of open d1 decision models built on LFM2.5
detail: Leonie reports that her team released its open d1 decision models this week, framing them as fast, multimodal models targeted at decision-making tasks rather than lengthy reasoning. The models build on the LFM2.5 model family, which the announcement credits with enabling fast decisions. An accompanying video discusses why fast multimodal decision models matter and what use cases they unlock.
developments.why_it_matters: The release makes fast, multimodal decision-making models openly available on the LFM2.5 base, giving developers a concrete open option for running quick multimodal decisions today.

developments.title: Mario Zechner Introduces Chat Mode for Steering Agents Without Queuing
detail: Mario Zechner introduced a chat mode for his agent tooling, framing it as a replacement for queuing messages while an agent is working.

In the new mode, a user mentions the agent, and the agent receives a single steering message containing all chat messages that had not been delivered up to that point, rather than commands piling up in a queue.
developments.why_it_matters: This changes how users correct a running agent: instead of queuing messages for later processing, a mention immediately delivers the agent a consolidated steering message with the full backlog of undelivered chat context.

developments.title: codex-switch: proxy pooling multiple Codex accounts
detail: A local Go proxy that aggregates multiple Codex subscriptions into a single shared pool.
Released under the MIT license, the tool is open source and works with any Codex harness.
developments.why_it_matters: Users can consolidate multiple Codex subscriptions, reducing per-user costs and simplifying usage management.

developments.title: Rat King: Encrypted AT Protocol Agent Network
detail: Joel Hooks announced Rat King, an open‑source encrypted AT Protocol‑based agent network that lets independent agents communicate over a federated layer. The repository includes support for message signing, peer‑to‑peer encryption, and deployment to Cloudflare or Celld for durable agents.

The companion Mis­chief repository provides durable XState‑machine plans stored as data and executed in Cloudflare Durable Objects, enabling resumable workflows and dynamic planning across the network.
developments.why_it_matters: It gives developers a ready‑made, secure infrastructure for building federated AI or automation agents that can run on Linux workstations or in the cloud today.

developments.title: Mario Zechner reports durable codemode achieved in pi agent tooling
detail: Mario Zechner reported that durable codemode has been achieved internally in his pi agent tooling, tying codemode execution to a durable execution layer he calls pi durable.

In follow-up commentary he indicated related capabilities fall directly out of that durable execution foundation, including dynamic workflows such as Claude Code's agents running durably with the ability to inspect and steer subagents.
The announcement is a brief status report without accompanying documentation, so the full scope of what durable codemode covers beyond codemode running on durable execution remains unclear.
developments.why_it_matters: Codemode execution in pi now runs on a durable execution base rather than an ephemeral one, and Zechner indicates related agent capabilities derive from pi durable rather than being separate mechanisms, though the full scope of what durable codemode enables has not been documented.

developments.title: GPT-6.1 Sol default context window raised to 500k in Codex and Work, with long-context premium reportedly removed
detail: The default context window for GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex and Work has reportedly been raised to 500k tokens, up from the previous 272k default, an increase of roughly 80%, while the maximum available context remains 1M and the default can still be overridden.

The change is described as carefully tested and positioned as the new sweet spot for most users, intended to reduce how often long-running sessions hit the compaction threshold and to better support tasks that need to retain substantial context and nuance over time.
Alongside the higher default, the long-context premium beyond 272k tokens has reportedly been removed, so the larger window carries no additional charge.
developments.why_it_matters: A higher default directly reduces how frequently long-running Codex and Work sessions require context compaction to stay within the window, and removing the premium beyond 272k means substantially larger code or document analyses can be run in a single request without extra charges, though both effects rest on reported claims rather than independent confirmation.

developments.title: agent-keyring workaround lets Claude run secret-dependent tasks without seeing credentials
detail: Josh reports a workaround for Claude's refusal to work directly with credentials: route the secrets through a password manager or his agent-keyring project instead of exposing them to the model. With the values kept out of view, Claude will proceed and carry out the requested task. The agent-keyring repository describes the project as controlled local access to Apple Passwords for AI agents on macOS.

One gap remains: the approach may not yet work with Claude's built-in browser, because Claude's tool calls need to read the credential value in order to write it there. Josh says he intends to try to fix that limitation.
developments.why_it_matters: Tasks that Claude otherwise stalls on over credential access can now be completed while the actual secrets stay in a local password store such as Apple Passwords, rather than being read into the model's context.
